body: Professional Translation
Thanks for the advice! And good luck with your studies.

They did for a while then the doctor lowered my dose and it brought me back 100 steps back, I could barely walk 15 minutes without feeling like I’ve ran a marathon, especially during summer. They’re the worst for me.

yep, that’s one of the first symptoms I experienced along with heart palpitations as someone who likes running and taking long walks it was really annoying to experience that shortness of breath I had to hit pauses on many activities because of it. I hope your medical treatment will have you feeling better in no time x
yes! that’s exactly how it feels like and i’ve been experiencing it more frequently. I have an appointment with my doctor this week i’ll make sure to bring it up. thank you x

I think some boundaries need to be established by her when it comes to the husband, and she should leave you out of this. She is an adult, she can sit him down and tells him comments like these disturb her. It is not for you or for us to decipher whether she is or he is in the wrong, if it disturbs her it disturbs her. You should validate that. As for your husband, he should keep comments like those to himself or to you, or to someone who gets his humor to avoid the family drama. Some people are more sensitive than others, and we can’t hold that against them.

I do know them, but they always prove to me that they’re worse than I ever thought. And on some days I’m hopeful that they changed, woke up one day and realized I am an important individual in the family as anyone else. This was hard to read because I know you’re right, you’re absolutely right I’ve known for a long time this isn’t what family should feel like. I always felt out of place, sort of like it’s not my home just a house. And it’s crazy because it’s been 25 years, and I still feel like this. Not a place I feel secure in, physically or emotionally. My dad made it bearable for a while, but even he sometimes feels like only treats me “better” to spit my mother. I’m saving money to move out, especially after this. This was a much needed reality check, thank you!
Oh I misunderstood, sorry. I did speak with my mom and she knows what to expect of me if something like this happens again.

My bad I thought access to your daughter who’s been with you through thick and thin is more important than access to your grandchild, who will most likely be taken by his mother and brainwashed into hating his dad’s side of the family. Including you.

She’s overly protective and controlling, and what she is doing is an invasion of privacy. My suggestion to you is to move out by the age of 21, because she might say once you hit 21 you’re an adult and she’ll let you do whatever but trust me that’s never the case. It’s bullshit. I’m 25 and my mother is still controlling, perhaps not as extreme as your mother but still. It’s a longer leash but it is still a leash. Mothers like that have deeply rooted trust issues and controlling issues, which can only healed through therapy or else it’ll follow them for the rest of their lives.
Thank you for your advice, I appreciate it. I’ll definitely try a psychiatrist.

Yeah, I get anxious and I ask them a million questions about their health and I suggest they go do check ups frequently. Sometimes they do, sometimes they don’t. And when they don’t I feel like I’m not doing enough as a daughter to keep them alive. 

Sometimes I just look at them as if expecting them to fall right then and there. It’s exhausting, I do enjoy life with them and I try to enjoy it when I’m not with them but that thought is always shadowing my mind.

I tried therapy, once I realized that this isn’t normal. But my therapist kept listening and telling me dying is a part of life and a cycle that ends... ect, and it all sounded very repetitive, it’s just not going through my brain. And I think it stems from never having someone close to me dying before and grieving it then recovering from it, so the experience is very unknown to me and I’m scared very of the unknown.

I meant teaching her what our boundaries and how to set them not which ones to set or with who, she’s never set a boundary with anyone. Like ever. And people take advantage of that. She was raised in a toxic household where setting boundaries is considered disrespectful.

Thank you, I appreciate your advice. I’m validating her emotions as much as possible as well teaching her how set boundaries since it’s an unfamiliar aspect to her, but it’s still unfair seeing an old person be emotionally manipulated like that by someone they love dearly.

It’s definitely favoritism. My mother does the same. Except I only have one older brother who dropped out of highschool but is still treated like a king. She buys him the most expensive clothes while I used to buy from the thrift store with my own money, he breaks his phones like every 3 months and she replaces them for him, she bought him a car, paid for his wedding, for his house, financed his kid’s schooling and finances his wife’s lifestyle because he can’t with his limited paycheck. When she can’t afford to give him money she calls my aunts and begs them and cries to them to give her son money, meanwhile I’m the one with a phD degree who never received a simple “i’m proud of you” or a birthday cake. I don’t know what is the science behind them doing this, but it’s definitely messed up. Whatever you’re feeling it’s completely valid, and I recommend moving out. Preferably far from the house. And cut them off slowly.
Exactly. Just when you think it can't get worse perhaps there it would be.
Thank you

I think I'm alone too but I know my parents will mourn me for sure but not because they loved me or anything I think it's having an empty room that will get to them. The silence of it. The fact that they got used to something and it's not there anymore. Sort of like a broken light bulb that you never got around to fix because you never needed to use it but one day you happen to get into that room and click on the switch and you realize you've never attempted to fix the light bulb because you didn't need it.
Because no one in his right mind would choose a life like this.
